item.title: Go Daily Question 20250516
item.description:
Which options A, B, C, D have syntax errors?

type S struct {
}

func f(x interface{}) {
}

func g(x *interface{}) {
}

func main() {
       s := S{}
       p := &s
       f(s) //A
       g(s) //B
       f(p) //C
       g(p) //D
}
🔑 Answer Analysis:

BD Run online

When a function parameter is interface{}, it can accept any type of argument, including user-defined types. Even when accepting a pointer type, interface{} should be used, not *interface{}.

item.title: Go Daily Question 140
item.description:
What is the output of the following code?

func main() {  
    var i interface{}
    if i == nil {
        fmt.Println("nil")
        return
    }
    fmt.Println("not nil")
}
  • A. nil
  • B. not nil
  • C. compilation error
    🔑 Answer Analysis:

    A Run online

    Simply put, an interface variable has two values: one is its type, and the other is its value. For an if interface, the live() == nil condition is true only when both the value and the type are zero values.
